missions.name: Latium - The Founding
missions.blurb: A strip of land by a river in Latium, a grant from the Senate, and a few families with nowhere else to go.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings.

The Senate has voted you the land below my estates, from the ford to the bend in the river. It is good soil and nobody lives on it, which tells you something about the floods. Families from the hills will come if there are houses and water. My steward will send what grain we can spare.

I put your name forward because you work and you do not complain. Do both there.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
Three hundred people live inside Spurinna's furrow. The ford has a road, the road has a market, and the Latin villages have started to call the place by a name.

A letter comes from Postumius. Rome is building a port at the mouth of the Tiber and needs a man to run its council. He has suggested you. Several senators had suggested their nephews.

missions.name: Ostia - River Port
missions.blurb: Rome's port at the mouth of the Tiber: salt pans, fishing boats, and a council that needs someone to run it.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings.

You will sit on the council at Ostia. In practice you will be the council: the others own warehouses in Rome and visit when the weather is good. The harbor master tells me the salt pans are the best on the coast and the fishermen the worst drunks.

Rome eats what comes up this river. See that it keeps coming.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
Ostia has quays, warehouses and a salt trade, and Rome eats a little better for it. The harbor master has stopped calling you the new man and started calling you the decurion.

The Senate sends you to the Samnite hills next. Calidius brings a second letter, unsealed. Lucius Aurunculeius Mela, whose father sits in the Senate, wanted that post for himself and said so in the Curia. "He will not forget it," Calidius says. "Neither will his father."

missions.name: Beneventum - Samnite Frontier
missions.blurb: A frontier town in the Samnite hills. The Samnites lost the last war and have not accepted it.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings.

The Samnites called that town Maleventum, the place of the bad wind. We renamed it when we took it. Now we have to deserve the new name.

Quintus Labienus will join you. He fought in those hills when you were learning to walk, and he will tell you so.

Young Mela made a speech against your appointment. It was a good speech. Make it look foolish.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
The Samnites send envoys instead of warbands. They walk in through the gate, look for a long time at the temple of Mars, and accept the treaty without much argument. Labienus says that is the best kind of battle.

Spurinna watches the birds over the hills for a whole morning and declares the wind good. Postumius writes that Campania needs a quaestor who cannot be bought with wine, and that he has assumed you qualify.

missions.name: Capua - Campania
missions.blurb: The richest soil in Italy and the softest city in it. Oil, wine, and nobles who expect to be flattered.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings.

Capua is rich. Its olives are fat, its wine is sweet, and its nobles think Rome is a provincial town that got lucky. Hannibal's army wintered there once and never fought as well again. Do not winter there.

The equites will build fine houses if you give them pleasant streets to build in. Rome wants their oil and their wine, and so, I imagine, will you.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
Capua's oil and wine go up the Appian Way every week, and the equites who laughed at your accent now ask you to dinner. You eat little and drink less. Postumius hears of it and approves.

The next letter carries the Senate's seal. Sicily feeds Rome, Syracuse is its greatest port, and the last aedile there spent more on his villa than on the harbor. The post is yours.

missions.name: Syracuse - Sicilia
missions.blurb: Archimedes' city, and Rome's granary. Wheat, garum, and ships that must not stop sailing.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings.

Sicilian wheat feeds Rome. When the ships are late the price of bread doubles, the crowds come out, and senators who never think about bread think about it very hard. Keep the ships sailing.

Your predecessor built himself a villa and a reputation. Build Rome a harbor.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
The harbor is a forest of masts and the warehouses smell of wheat and fish sauce. When the grain fleet sails, the bakers of Rome stop worrying.

Before you leave, Vitruvius takes you to Archimedes' tomb by the Agrigentine gate. He has had a stone bench set in front of it. "For the next one who comes looking," he says.

The Senate's next letter is short. Scipio has taken New Carthage in Spain, with its silver mines, and someone has to hold it.

missions.name: Carthago Nova - Hispania
missions.blurb: Scipio took New Carthage and its silver mines. Carthage wants them back.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings.

The hills behind New Carthage are full of silver, and forty thousand men dig it out. That silver pays our legions. Carthage knows this as well as we do, and its armies are still in Spain.

Build mines and forges, raise real legions, and hold the city. Labienus will enjoy it more than you will.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
The last Punic army in Spain is beaten in the hills west of the city. Labienus brings back a Carthaginian helmet and sets it on a shelf in the praetorium, next to a Samnite one.

The mines run, the forges run, and Rome pays its legions in Spanish silver. Postumius writes that the Senate is founding a city at the head of the Adriatic, where the Alps come down to the sea, and that it will need water, walls, and someone who can manage both.

missions.name: Aquileia - Northern Frontier
missions.blurb: The gate to the north at the foot of the Alps. Raiders in the passes, and a city that needs running water.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings.

Aquileia guards the road over the Alps. Gauls and Illyrians come down the passes when they are hungry, and in that country they are hungry every winter.

It will be a large city, and large cities need water brought in from the hills. Your engineer will be happy at last.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
Water comes down from the hills into the reservoir, through the pipes and out of the fountains, and people stop in the street to watch it. Vitruvius stands at the first fountain for most of a morning. Back at his desk he rewrites the chapter on water for the third time.

The raiders have learned that Aquileia has walls, forts and a garrison that never sleeps. Postumius sends you west, to Gaul, where a new road crosses an old trade route.

missions.name: Narbo Martius - Gallia
missions.blurb: Where the road from Italy meets the roads to Spain and Gaul. Make it the market of the West.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings.

Narbo is a crossroads. The Via Domitia runs through it to Spain, the river runs to the sea, and the tracks into Gaul lead to tribes who would rather trade with us than fight, as long as we have wine.

One warning. The legion in Gaul is commanded by Lucius Mela, a praetor now like you. He will need supplies from you, and he will enjoy asking.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
Narbo's market sells Spanish silver, Gaulish wool, Italian wine and Greek pottery, and takes a small tax on all of it. Mela's legion is fed, dry and supplied, and his letters have grown shorter.

Postumius writes from Rome in an unsteady hand. A gladiator called Spartacus has broken out of a school in Capua, and the slaves of Campania are going over to him by the thousand. The Senate is making you consul and sending you there.

missions.name: Campania - The Servile War
missions.blurb: A gladiator named Spartacus has escaped from Capua, and the slaves of Campania are going over to him.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings.

You are consul. I had hoped to see it in better times.

Spartacus has beaten two Roman armies. The estates of Campania are worked by slaves, and every one of them has heard his name. The Senate wants order. Hold the city, hold the roads, and if you can, keep the slaves from joining him. Crassus is raising legions and will come, eventually.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
Crassus's legions catch Spartacus at last, far to the south, and he dies fighting. Six thousand prisoners are crucified along the Appian Way, from Capua to Rome, one every forty paces. Lollius rides part of the road and comes back without speaking.

The city held. Postumius sends congratulations and very little else. The Republic is tearing itself apart, and there are armies in the streets of Rome that belong to men, not to the Senate. One of those men, Caesar, has ordered Corinth rebuilt. You are to build it.

missions.name: Corinth - Refounded
missions.blurb: A century after Rome burned Corinth, Caesar orders it rebuilt with freedmen and veterans.
missions.letter:
Aulus Postumius sends greetings, for what may be the last time.

I am old, and the doctors have stopped pretending otherwise. I wanted you to have Corinth from my hand while my hand still counts for something.

Rome burned Corinth a hundred years ago and sold its people. Caesar is building it again with freedmen and veterans, and Greek learning never entirely left. Build schools there, and a theater, and let the Greeks argue in it.

You were the best thing I did in the Senate.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
Corinth has a market again, an odeon full of Greeks arguing, and an academy where the arguments are written down. The freedmen who came here a few years ago now call themselves Corinthians.

The next letter is not from Postumius, and it is not from the Senate. It comes from the office of Caesar's heir, in a polite and careful hand: Lugdunum in Gaul needs a governor who knows how to build.

missions.name: Lugdunum - Capital of Gaul
missions.blurb: The capital of the Three Gauls, in the years the Republic becomes an Empire.
missions.letter:
From the office of Gaius Julius Caesar Octavianus, to the proconsul. Greetings.

Lugdunum stands where the Rhodanus meets the Arar. It is to be the capital of the Three Gauls. Its hills hold silver. Strike it into coin, honour the gods of Rome, and show the chiefs of Gaul what Rome looks like when it is generous.

Reports are to be sent to this office monthly.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
The chiefs of the Three Gauls meet at Lugdunum, walk under your arch, and pay their taxes in coins from your mint with the Emperor's head on them. Calidius keeps one of the first coins in his purse and does not spend it.

The palace sends you to Egypt. Egypt belongs to the Emperor personally, the letter explains, and no senator may set foot in it without his permission. You have his permission.

missions.name: Alexandria - Egypt
missions.blurb: The Emperor's own province: the Nile, the grain fleet, and the lighthouse on Pharos.
missions.letter:
From the office of the Emperor, to the governor of Alexandria. Greetings.

Egypt is the Emperor's personal estate, and a third of Rome's grain comes from it. Each summer the Nile floods, renews the fields, and soaks everything foolish enough to be built on them.

The Emperor wishes the light on Pharos to burn again, and the people of Alexandria to have a circus, so that they cheer for chariots and not for pretenders.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
The light burns on Pharos again, and ships coming in at night steer by it from forty miles out. The circus is full every race day, and the crowd shouts for the Greens and the Blues instead of against the governor.

The palace's next letter sends you north, to the Rhine. It mentions, in one dry sentence, that three legions were lost in the German forests not long ago and that their eagles were never found.

missions.name: Colonia Agrippina - The Rhine
missions.blurb: The Rhine frontier: forts, siege engines, and winters that close the roads.
missions.letter:
From the office of the Emperor, to his legate on the Rhine. Greetings.

The Rhine is the edge of the world Rome governs. The tribes on the far bank test it every year, and every year it must hold. Colonia is to be the anchor of the frontier, a city of forts, granaries and engines of war.

The Emperor's confidence goes with you. So do two more legions, on paper.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
The tribes stop crossing. Their chiefs come down to the far bank under a green branch and ask for a market instead, and you give them one, on this side of the river, where you can watch it.

Labienus's shoulder has healed badly, and he no longer pretends otherwise. He asks for one more posting with you, and then a farm. The palace sends you to Britannia, to a new town on the Thames that is growing too fast.

missions.name: Londinium - Britannia
missions.blurb: A new trading town on the Thames, growing fast among Britons who never asked for it.
missions.letter:
From the office of the Emperor, to his legate in Britannia. Greetings.

Londinium is a merchants' town on the Thames, new and growing quickly. The governor is campaigning in the far west, on the island of Mona, and the eastern tribes are quiet.

The Emperor would like them to remain quiet.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
Londinium rises again in brick and stone, along a river crowded with ships. Under the new forum the workmen dig through a layer of black earth full of melted glass and fused coins, and build on top of it.

Labienus reminds you about the farm. You promise it to him after one more posting, and he says he has heard that before. The next letter sends you east, to Antioch, as prefect.

missions.name: Antioch - The East
missions.blurb: The Queen of the East: caravans from Parthia and India, theatres, luxury, and a city built on a fault.
missions.letter:
From the office of the Emperor, to the prefect of Antioch. Greetings.

Antioch is the third city of the empire, where the caravans of Parthia and India meet the ships of the sea. The governor of Syria is Lucius Aurunculeius Mela. The Emperor trusts that two of his servants can work together.

The Empress has asked for Antiochene jewelry.

Farewell.
missions.victory:
Antioch is rebuilt, its colonnades straighter than before and its markets louder. Caravans come in out of the desert and leave with glass and purple.

Before you leave, a letter arrives from the palace. Rome has burned. Ten of its fourteen districts are ash, and the Emperor wants the man who rebuilt Antioch to rebuild the City. Mela's recommendation is enclosed. It is four lines long, and it calls you the best builder in the empire. Calidius holds it up to the lamp, looking for the trick.

missions.name: Roma - Caput Mundi
missions.blurb: Rome after the great fire: ten of its fourteen districts in ashes, and the whole world watching.
missions.letter:
From the Emperor, to the Prefect of the City. Greetings.

Nine days of fire have left ten of Rome's fourteen districts in ashes. The people sleep in the parks, and the temples are smoking shells.

Rebuild Rome greater than it was: an amphitheatre to outshine every other, a temple to all the gods, and the greatest circus in the world. The treasury will help you.

Do not make me regret it.
missions.epilogue:
The Colosseum fills with fifty thousand people who came to see blood and stay to look at the building. The dome of the Pantheon hangs over the city with a hole at the top for the gods to look in. The Circus Maximus holds more people than lived in Capua.

Vitruvius finishes his ten books on architecture. He dedicates them to the Emperor, and your name is in the preface, spelled correctly.

Calidius closes the accounts of the rebuilding. They balance to the last as. He retires to Ostia and buys a share in a salt works.

Lollius stays on as aedile under the next prefect. On market days he still walks the streets and listens.

Labienus has his farm at last, by the river in Latium, a short walk from the stone Spurinna set at the founding. He grows bad wine and tells the neighbours about the Rhine.

Spurinna takes the auspices on the Capitol one last time. He watches the sky for a long while and will not say what he saw.

The hamlet by the ford is a town of four thousand now. The first stone still stands at the edge of its forum, and someone has cut your name into it.
